meta.parties: Kirihamy v. Kiri Banda Et Al

rules.statement: A person who has knowledge of a prior unregistered conveyance and still registers their own conveyance does not necessarily commit fraud under the provisions of Ordinance No. 14 of 1891, as long as they did not engage in any fraudulent acts during the registration process itself.
rules.supporting_quote: "Each party is standing on his legal right, and we find no grounds on which we can say that either has been trying to mislead the other. The first mortgagee must be taken to have known that if he did not register his incumbrance a second mortgagee might step in before him. All that is proved respecting 1 the second mortgagee is that, knowing of the first mortgage, he took the legal steps to secure himself: he is not shown to have done anything underhand or to have made any pretence."
